title: Patch: stepping back in a replay or flipping the co-op portal keeps the match's music, instead of starting the next track as if a new match began
thread:
**Issue #4606 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4606: Patch: stepping back in a replay or flipping the co-op portal keeps the match's music, instead of starting the next track as if a new match began
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In a replay, stepping back one move, dragging the scrubber or jumping to an earlier turn makes the music act as if a brand-new match had started. The in-game track fades out, the menu theme often plays for a few seconds, and then a different in-game track starts from its beginning. Near the start of a game the match-start fanfare plays again. In a co-op game on a phone, where one board shows at a time, every flip between your board and your teammate's does the same. Each of these moves also advances the device's track rotation, so the next real match plays an arbitrary track. Stepping forward one move is already fine.

Once this is built, the music carries on across those moves as it does on a step forward. Opening another replay, or starting a new match, still moves on to the next track.

## Why

- **Backward replay moves remount the board.** Any move that is not one step forward gives the board a new key (`apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.tsx:129-132`). `<Game key={at.board}>` then mounts afresh (`ReplayPlayer.tsx:274`).
- **Portal flips remount too.** The co-op single-board layout swaps `key="board-own"` and `key="board-teammate"` on each flip (`duos/DuosBoard.tsx:599-629`).
- **Each mount starts music as a new match.** Every mount enters the game music and builds a new music director (`audio/useGameAudio.ts:156-170`). Every unmount's `leave()` hands the music back, and `apply()` asks for the menu theme while a menu screen holds it (`audio/musicScene.ts:15-27`, `79-84`).
- **The rotation is keyed on a view object.** `rotationFor(first)` (`audio/musicDirector.ts:63-73`) looks the rotation up in a `WeakMap` by the first view object. A remount brings a new view object, so `nextRotation()` advances the stored counter `jackioh.music.rotation.v1` (`audio/musicData.ts:125-128`) and picks the next track.
- **The first view resets the track.** The director's first `onView` clears the resume points and, at `turn <= 1`, asks for the match-start sting (`musicDirector.ts:182-191`). If the new track is not decoded yet, the menu theme keeps playing until it is (`audio/music.ts:490-501`).
- **The guard covers a different case.** The `WeakMap` only guards React's StrictMode double mount on the same view (its comment, `musicDirector.ts:66-67`).
- **It breaks the spec.** SPEC §10.11 (R631) rotates the in-game tracks "from match to match". A replay step and a portal flip are not new matches.
- **No test catches it.** The director's tests never mount a second board of the same match.

## Proposal

1. **Hold one music key per match.** `ReplayPlayer` and `DuosBoard` each hold a key for their whole life: one replay, or one co-op match. Each passes it through a new optional `Game` prop to `useGameAudio`.
2. **Reuse the existing seam.** `useGameAudio` passes the key to `createMusicDirector`, which already takes a `rotation` option. The rotation comes from the key, so a remount under the same key gets the same rotation. The director clears the resume points and asks for the start sting only on the key's first mount. A remount continues the track it was playing.
3. **No menu theme between two boards.** When one board leaves and another enters in the same commit, the music passes from one to the other without requesting the menu theme in between. For example, `leave()` can defer its `apply()` until after the entering board has made its claim. A board leaving with nothing after it still brings the menu theme back.
4. **Boards without a key are unchanged.** Live match, practice, daily, dungeon and hotseat boards behave exactly as today.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.tsx`, `apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.tsx` (hold and pass the key)
- `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx` (one optional prop to `useGameAudio`)
- `apps/web/src/audio/useGameAudio.ts`, `audio/musicDirector.ts`, `audio/musicScene.ts`
- Tests: `replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx`, a DuosBoard test, `audio/musicDirector.test.ts`, `audio/musicScene` (or `wiring.test.tsx`)
- SPEC §10.11: a ruling note in the issue's block, amending R631 (a replay or a co-op match is one match however often its board remounts). Its §11 paragraph goes in `spec/pending/<issue>.md`, and the note lists its proving test.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replay: open a replay, step forward, back, jump with the scrubber and by turn. Afterwards `jackioh.music.rotation.v1` is where opening the replay left it, and the music player's wanted track is the same throughout.
- [ ] Replay: the menu theme is never requested between those moves, the track's resume point is kept, and the match-start sting plays at most once.
- [ ] Co-op: in a single-board DuosBoard test, flipping the portal back and forth leaves the rotation and the wanted track as they were.
- [ ] A different replay, or a new match, still moves the rotation on once.
- [ ] A board leaving to a menu with no board after it still brings the menu theme back.
- [ ] Live match, practice and hotseat boards behave as before, and the existing audio tests pass.
- [ ] The ruling note's proving test is named after it, and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

## Size and risks

Medium: about six source files and four test files in `apps/web/src`, plus one ruling note and its pending paragraph. No engine, server or wire change; presentation only (CLAUDE.md rule 7). The main risk is in point 3: deferring the hand-back touches every board's exit. A test should hold that a real exit still plays the menu theme, and that a hotseat hand-over (no remount) is unchanged.

|---|---|---|

| `apps/web/src/audio/musicDirector.test.ts` | change | `rig` gains `musicKey`; new `R4606000` remount tests |
| `apps/web/src/audio/music-ui.test.tsx` | change | Flush microtasks after unmount; new `R4606000` handoff/exit tests |

2. Same file, `createMusicDirector`: add `const key = options.musicKey;` and `const rotationOf = options.rotation ?? (key !== undefined ? () => rotationForKey(key) : rotationFor);` replacing the current `rotationOf` line. In `onView`'s `if (viewer === null)` branch, compute `const fresh = key === undefined ? true : !startedMusicKeys.has(key);` then `if (key !== undefined) startedMusicKeys.add(key);`. 3. `apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.ts`: add `let applyQueued = false;` and `function scheduleApply(): void { if (applyQueued) return; applyQueued = true; queueMicrotask(() => { applyQueued = false; apply(); }); }`. In `leave()`, replace the trailing `apply()` with `scheduleApply()`. Leave `request()` and `holdMenuMusic` synchronous. Effect: an unmount followed by a mount in the same commit never requests the menu theme; a real exit requests it on the microtask.
4. `apps/web/src/audio/useGameAudio.ts`: change the signature to `export function useGameAudio(runner: AnimationQueue, view: PlayerView, silent = false, musicKey?: object): void` and change the director creation to `musicRef.current = createMusicDirector({ sink, musicKey });` (passing `musicKey: undefined` when absent preserves current behavior).
5. `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx`: add to `GameProps` after `silent?: boolean;` the field `/** R4606000: one object per match; remounts under the same key keep the match's music. Absent, every mount is a new match. */ musicKey?: object;`, add `musicKey` to the destructuring, and change the line 571 call to `useGameAudio(runner, view, silent, musicKey);`.
6. `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.tsx`: add `const musicKey = useMemo(() => ({}), [source]);` next to the `cache` memo (same dependency, so a different replay is a different key), and pass `musicKey={musicKey}` to the `Game` element. Do not change the `key={at.board}` logic.
7. `apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.tsx`: add `const musicKey = useMemo(() => ({}), []);` near the other state (one key per mounted co-op match), and pass `musicKey={musicKey}` to every `Game` it renders (both-layout own board, single-board own branch, single-board teammate branch; the silent teammate board's hook returns early so the key is inert there). Do not change any `key=` values.
8. `apps/web/src/audio/music-ui.test.tsx`: existing tests assert the menu theme synchronously after `unmount()`. After step 3 they must flush the microtask first: make those tests `async` and insert `await act(async () => {});` between `unmount()` and the menu-theme assertion (`act` is already imported). Keep every assertion; this is timing, not weakening. Grep for `track: "menu"` in `apps/web/src/audio/*.test.*` and `wiring.test.tsx` and flush anywhere a menu assertion follows an unmount in the same tick.
9. Ruling docs: write `spec/rulings/R4606000.md` (front matter `id: R4606000`, title naming the replay/portal remount rule, `cards: "§10.11, R631, issue #4606"`, `proven_in` listing the four test files from the table; body: a replay step that remounts and a co-op portal flip are the same match — same rotation, same wanted track, resume kept, start sting at most once, no menu theme between boards; a different replay or new match advances once; a real exit returns the menu theme; presentation only per rule 7). Write `spec/pending/4606.md` holding the one §11 paragraph in the surrounding paragraphs' style: `**[[R4606000]] … (issue #4606, 2026-11-23)**: …`, amending `[[R631]]`.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/audio/musicDirector.test.ts`: extend `rig` options with `musicKey?: object` and build the director with `...(options.musicKey === undefined ? { rotation: () => options.rotation ?? 0 } : { musicKey: options.musicKey })`. Add `it("R4606000 a remount under the same music key keeps the rotation and asks for no sting", …)`: clear `MUSIC_ROTATION_KEY`, `key = {}`, first rig `onView(opening())` gives `tavern-1` with `intro: "tavern-start"` and one reset; dispose; second rig with the same key `onView(midGame())` gives `tavern-1` with `intro: null` and zero resets; `localStorage` counter is `"1"`. Add `it("R4606000 a different music key moves the rotation on", …)`: a second key's first view gives `tavern-2` with the sting and counter `"2"`.
- `apps/web/src/audio/music-ui.test.tsx`: add `it("R4606000 two boards of one match in a single commit never ask for the menu theme", …)`: render `<Game … musicKey={key}/>`, unmount, synchronously render `<Game … musicKey={key}/>`, flush microtasks, assert no request after the first game request has `track: "menu"` and both game requests want the same track. Add `it("R4606000 a keyed board leaving with nothing after it still brings the menu theme back", …)`: with `holdMenuMusic()`, render, unmount, flush, assert the last request is `{ track: "menu", opponentTurn: false }`.
- `apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx`: add `it("R4606000 stepping back, scrubbing and jumping turns keeps the rotation and the wanted track", …)`: copy the file's `recordingPlayer` pattern from `music-ui.test.tsx` with `setMusicPlayerForTests`, top-level `await loadSoundTables()`, `localStorage.clear()` in `beforeEach`. Open the fake replay, `flush()`, record rotation value and wanted track; then `press` back-step, forward-step, `jump` via the scrubber, back-turn and forward-turn buttons (test ids `replay-back-step`, `replay-forward-step`, `replay-scrubber`, `replay-back-turn`, `replay-forward-turn`), flushing each time. Assert the rotation value is unchanged throughout, the wanted track is unchanged throughout, no request after the first game request names `"menu"`, and at most one request carries a non-null `intro`.
- `apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.test.tsx`: add `it("R4606000 flipping the portal back and forth keeps the rotation and the wanted track", …)`: same recording-player setup; `renderDuosBoard()` default single-board view; record rotation and wanted track; call the file's `flipPortal()` twice; assert rotation and wanted track unchanged, no `"menu"` request, at most one request with non-null `intro`.
- Commands: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/audio/musicDirector.test.ts`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/audio/music-ui.test.tsx`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/replay/ReplayPlayer.test.tsx`, `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/duos/DuosBoard.test.tsx`, then `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck`, `pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/audio/musicDirector.ts apps/web/src/audio/musicScene.ts apps/web/src/audio/useGameAudio.ts apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx apps/web/src/replay/ReplayPlayer.tsx apps/web/src/duos/DuosBoard.tsx`, then `cargo jackioh spec check`.

## Done when

- [ ] Backward replay moves and portal flips keep rotation, wanted track, resume point; sting at most once; no menu request between boards.
- [ ] A different replay and a new match each advance the rotation once.
- [ ] A real exit to a menu still requests the menu theme; hotseat hand-over (no remount) unchanged.
- [ ] Keyless live/practice/hotseat boards behave as before; all touched web test files pass.
- [ ] `R4606000` proving tests exist in all four `proven_in` files and `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

## Risks

- Deferred `leave()` touches every board's exit: the updated `R631` hand-back tests plus the new real-exit test pin it; a missed sync-unmount assertion shows up as a menu request one microtask late, fixed by flushing, never by dropping the assertion.
- The new director keeps no per-key station map: a remount recomputes from settings, so a mid-match station switch made by a cast event is forgotten by the remount. Acceptable here because the proving cases hold the station constant; note it as a rejected alternative (persisting stations per key) to keep the change minimal.
- Object-identity keys rely on `ReplayPlayer` staying mounted across steps (true: only `Game`'s key changes) and `DuosBoard` remounting per match via its route; `useMemo(..., [source])` ties the replay key to the replay the route keys the player by.

## Open questions

None. All choices are settled by the issue's proposal and the repo's conventions.
```
